author: nomaddc
quote:
A game that not only doesn't work as one would expect a game in 2026 to work, but also under delivers and in many ways betrays the fans.
Atrocious performance, we are still being told that 30fps "target" is an acceptable video game performance in 2026, but it doesn't stop there - there are of course bugs, lots. Cyberpunk 2077 got a lot more flak for a messy launch, and while it's comparable here we see a lot of people coming out to let us know that we should not trust our lying eyes and ears.
Narrative is... bad, even for a GTA game. Gone is the fire it had for merciless satire of modernity, now it's safer, more equitable, with soft and rounded corners. Instead of a compelling but ultimately tragic criminal story we get a girlfriend simulator disguised as a boyfriend simulator, where Jason is just the right kind of imaginary bf for all the players (do they exist?) who can see themselves in a feisty latina. Good on you, at least someone is getting what they have wanted.

It's a step down even from GTA V - bouncy airplanes, unstealable cars, restrictions on who you can fire an imaginary gun at. But hey, you can work out now and paint walls!

The monetization is there to stay - GTA plus has wormed its way even into single player, so you can be sure there are plans for when the Online part of the game comes (if it will at this point).

Overall, if you enjoy the current thing, but want to still maintain a sort of image of a free thinker and a rebel, and be edgy because the news lady is freaking out yet again about your favorite game (are we sure it's not a weird paid marketing campaign? Every damn time a GTA comes out they roll them put) then this is for you. A nice change of pace from Madden/CoD and your other favorite gacha/gamba/annual slop that you can consume and wear proudly as your gamer badge.

author: nomaddc
quote:
A great DLC that goes ways towards addressing many of the base game issues, but is somewhat held back by the base game being a lesser of the two parts.
While I do like the original Dark Arisen for DD1 better, this is still great and has been a blast, and I can wholeheartedly recommend it as money well spent if you already own DD2 and/or have already played the heck out of the original. author: nomaddc
quote:
After spending some hours in the latest version of the game with DLC1&2, I've decided to update this a bit. The game is still just bad. While they have done some tweaking and shifting for balance, it largely remains a joke/superfluous because the game plays like the worst version of cRPG rocket tag - you just make sure you go first and there's no turn 2. The rpg system is still just as bloated and obtuse, with some unclear rules and language here and there.

The game loves loading screens, they are everywhere. Going from a location to the map where you can travel somewhere is 2 loading screens, sometimes 3. Going almost anywhere on the ship is a loading screen. Going from the ship to the map is a loading screen. Going from the system map to the larger map is a loading screen. Space combat - loading screens in and out. Warp events - same deal or pay resources to skip. And the loading screens are unnaturally long without mods that thankfully fix them.

A large bit of problem with the game is that something like 70% of your build is hidden and locked away from you in items you find (or not) as the game goes on, which means you either start your builds with an open wiki and hope it has all the items and their locations, or you just make peace with that you'll be making a build pretty much blind and will most likely have to nuke it a few times as the game goes on. It still goes with the silly restrictive weapon proficiencies to use such staples as plasma, melta, and bolters, while also giving everyone but your character 3-4 free traits. So on early levels you're quite likely to be the weakest member of your party, and if you need/want those proficiencies you will never be able to catch up to them, just because they get some parts of their build simply for free while you don't.

The writing is at best very uneven. There are decently written plotlines and dialogues, and then there's awful grimderp level writing. The writers often write in cruelty and bad outcomes just for the sake of it, not for some logical (using 40k logic, naturally) or at least understandable reason. Some characters like a certain Inquisitor are written so poorly it became a joke that Ordo Xenos trained him wrong, as a joke, due to his incompetency as an inquisitor/unwillingness to share information to avoid horrible consequences (avoiding which is kind of part of the job?). 

Alignment system is rather dumb and limiting, forcing you into 3 buckets - Heretical, Dogmatic, and Iconoclast. Heretical has is the less problem ridden one of the 3, but it's written almost purely in the "groveling slave" fantasy, so if you want to play a heretical character with some dignity/had other ideas on how to RP a heretical rogue trader - tough luck, bucko. Dogmatic and Iconoclast basically are at odds because writers position them often (but not always) as "Jerk and sadist" vs "Nice", but also "Will magically avoid bad consequences" and "will get bad consequences". While yes, a lot of "nice" choices do naturally lead to bad outcomes in 40k - thinking sparing mutants and such - it is not universally so and some things you get punished for are just arbitrary. Besides, Iconoclast is written to be heretical to the Imperium, so there's that. There's no reason why not roleplaying a deranged commissar that shoots subordinates for spilling his recaf should lead to "Imperium considers you a dangerous heretic". Conversely, Dogmatic usually leads to better outcomes, but with the gusto of uncalled for cruelty and imbecilic behavior. It's the same amount of points to Exterminatus a demon world in the making, and to shoot a poor officer who happened to take command on a besieged world for "not winning hard enough". In the end the conflict here lies in that these are poor categories and sensible, loyal to Imperium choices are about 40/60 Dogmatic/Iconoclast, and heretical or plain stupid/sadistic are the rest. But the game wants you to do the exact opposite - they want you to go full blast for just 1 - you lock in after a number of points is accumulated and that then locks progression in other alignments and also locks some of the dialogue options. What happens if you've been roughly 50/50? Well, whichever happens to tip over first wins, congrats you're now locked. This is one of the worst alignment systems I've seen.

The system itself also does a spectacularly poor job of representing 40k lore. Welcome to the world where an Inferno Pistol shot is just minor discomfort, bolter shells are comparable to autogun rounds, and the thing separating power sword from a primitive sword is like 10 armor pen and an inconsequential bonus. Plasma pistols are pea shooters now, and overheating a plasma gun is something everyone on your team can just walk off. Melta guns (yes, the anti-tank weapons) tickle humanoid enemies at point blank. You feeling 40k yet?

author: nomaddc
quote: This used to be a promising game until the company leadership decided it's time to squeeze the players for money. They are far from first in the industry, but they seem to be set on becoming the most comprehensive in implementing as many predatory and poor monetization practices as one can. They have released a separate arena style game that is required to use one of the traders in Tarkov itself. They have come out with an awful battle pass, that follows some of the worst battle pass practices with daily limits on progression and convoluted point system to even advance through levels, naturally the $100 bribe can make it all go away. They have added seasons but made them strictly PvP while telling PvE players to sock it, and put exclusive gear and items behind seasons, which I suppose PvE players are supposed to just do without. They have a massive backlog of unreleased guns, but now that we've seen the first battle pass - seems like these guns will only ever now come as parts of battle passes, so you better not miss the battlepass with the guns you want, or who knows how it'll be obtainable in the future.

author: nomaddc
quote:
This is what happens when the team behind a game desperately wants to make some sort of sociopolitical commentary, rather than a good sequel. Can't even say that it's technically unsound - performance is not bad in a decade marked by sloppy and poorly performing games. The real problem is the creative side of things, or I'd rather say creatively bankrupt side. Instead of good writing, compelling characters, grimdark fantasy, moral dillemas, you get a fortnite looking bunch of unlikeable characters and a feeling that HR is always in the room. Gone are meaningful dialogue options - you can only be positive and affirming as you get railroaded down the story. No more moral dillemas - that would ruin the happy good time you are supposed to be having. This is not a dragon age game, this is just a boilerplate fanfic written by a socially conscious youth that hadn't had a chance to experience the world outside their little bubble. Which is not surprising - as a generation of uninteresting and idle people who instead of experiencing life to the fullest turn inwards and focus on how they can stand out of a legion of similar idle and uninteresting through their "identity" - they can't come up with anything even nearing the original games, and ironically lack any and all identity of their own.

Out goes the grimdark, in goes the HR.

How many times do we have to teach this lesson, games industry?

author: nomaddc
quote:
I have not finished beating the game yet, but here what I can say so far:
- Story is compelling and captivating enough for me to enjoy it.
- A lot of good UI additions, such as in-cutscene access to lore.
- Combat is easy to pick up, but has a nice amount of depth.
- That said I'm not sure that will last until the end, combat is getting rather repetitive and new batches of abilities don't seem to be enough to keep it fun and interesting.
- Performance is horrible for the level of graphics they have. Performance mode makes it even worse without giving even a stable 60fps. God of War Ragnarok had much more compelling graphical fidelity while also running fairly well on performance mode, for comparison. FF16 perf is insulting and is easily why I took off 2 points.
- It is a departure from the classics in almost every way.
- There is no party really.
- Equipment is rather uninspired and boring, with amulets maybe being the highlight and we're talking here about an exciting "X ability does 10% more damage".
- You also only get to equip the main character.
- Only weapon has visuals, rest of the gear does not change the character look.
- I feel like I would rather have something closer to FF6 gameplay, the action twist has not been working for mainline FF entries so far (IMO) and seems to still be a failure.
- Cutscenes are great, QTE are fine and don't (so far) get overused.
- Characters are interesting and a lot are well written.
- Most of the levels are extremely linear for better or worse.
- Open areas are a chore to explore early on because of all the running you have to do. This is addressed a bit further into the game, so I would suggest waiting with exploration until then.
- That said there's not all that much to explore.
- Side quests are hit or miss. Some are good and have nice little stories. Some are blatant fetch quests.

Overall I feel like it's a decent game, but it's nowhere near GOTY or 10/10. If they fix the performance I would give it back its 2 points and it would be a solid 7/10. It does what it sets off to do fairly well, still hits that FF story feel. I play these games mostly for the story, and that's the part that is good here too, hence potentially 7/10. Combat is really a miss I think, and RPG systems are shallow and disappointing, I doubt I will be replaying this one. I've expected more from the talented team behind it, especially since they seemed to have demonstrated in the past that they understand what is it that people like about older FF games. They don't. It's a bit sad to see FF slowly lose its JRPG DNA. There are way better action games out there, I don't understand why do they want to shoehorn themselves into this already overpopulated genre.

author: nomaddc
quote:
Absolutely amazing game. As someone who was not blown away by its predecessor that was starring William as the protagonist, I immediately fell in love with this one after the first mission. There's just something special in being able to make your own character. Also I personally enjoyed more the story of a character local to Japan rather than an Englishman form across the ocean (no hate on William though, he's great but not my cup of tea).

There is some legitimate criticism towards the PC port, namely the controls on KB+M. But in all fairness, I have tried playing all of the Souls titles that had PC releases (so 1-3, Sekiro, remasters) and honestly none of them were enjoyable on KB+M. Every single time I have ended up switching to a controller, and frankly I believe this genre simply plays better on a controller. So do yourself a favor and grab that x-box or ps4/5 (by the way, dualshock4 has flawless support in this game, it's one of not many games that recognized mine right away and had all the PS4 button prompts). Just don't torture yourself trying to force KB+M on this game.

DLSS was added in a recent patch and it's stellar. It allows me to run the game at pretty stable and smooth 120fps, while before it would chug a bit when particle effects appear in large quantities.

The story is fairly simple, but very well executed. I saw some people make an argument that they didn't like "silent protagonist" deal, and that's a valid opinion; in my opinion the protagonist is rather expressive in his/her body language, facial expressions and actions, so you don't really need a voice or lines of dialogue. It's fairly hard to nail a voiced protagonist for a player made character that would please everyone (or even the majority), so a silent but expressive protagonist that leaves some blanks for you to fill is the next logical step and IMO it works well.

Gameplay is crisp, there is a good variety in weapons and ways you can build your character, lots of stuff to farm and try after the main story is done. To me, Nioh 2 did what I wanted Sekiro to do - which is a punishing and difficult action/RPG set in feudal Japan, with character customization and different era accurate (and completely made up) weapons.

In the 2020 - February 2021 draught of good video games Nioh 2 is a lush oasis, with lovely story, characters, amazing gameplay and co-op (and I know it came out a while ago on console, but I don't currently own one, the review is for the PC version). While other sequels and new entries in the latest history have been anything in-between extremely disappointing and criminally unfinished, Nioh 2 surpassed it's predecessor and didn't need microtransactions, lootboxes or other scummy practices to excel.

The review above is my personal opinion. I definitely agree to some of the criticisms and am opent to discuss them, but I strongly believe that the "lack of DLSS" (false as of right now) or "bad graphics lol" are a valid reason to rate the game 0/10. If you are that immature that you gonna throw a temper tantrum over nothing and rate an otherwise with a score that would put it alongside the likes of Cyberpunk, Anthem, Andromeda, Battlefront 2 on release, etc. you have no business posting reviews.

author: nomaddc
quote:
It's an amazing Dragon Age entry. While it's not perfect in my opinion and may lack some of the freedom in character building Origins had, it makes up for it in other areas.

Its semi open world structure reminds of Origins larger areas that we got to explore, but with much less linearity. The world is not leveled, meaning some areas may be extremely dangerous for you depending on your progress and sometimes it may be wise to simply come back later than try to press on. In my opinion this is the way go instead of skyrimesque leveled world where everything tries to keep on the player's level which oftentimes results in mediocre or below challenge (especially considering how hard it is to balance such scaling against different playstyles). The game areas are beautiful, have plenty of quests to do, items to collect, but you won't find DA2's overabundance of fetch quests.

Crafting system is quite simple but nice - the power level of the items you create is determined by the materials you use, as well as various secondary stats and it's appearance. This system manages not only to make sense (to craft metal armor you need metal, obviously, leather for all the leather bits or cloth, depending on the schematic and design) but also provide you with lots of options when trying to make an armor set or a weapon for your specific needs. The only shortcoming of this system in my opinion is that if you don't like the look of the customizable armor (that on top of different crafting components supports various mods) you will be left with a limited amount of unique armors that are not as customizable and some of them can't be crafted. That said, there is a good amount of those and good variety. My only wish for this part of the game is to have more unique endgame armor sets that rival or even surpass crafted, because that would make getting those unique pieces oh so more special.

Combat is very RPG like. It may be good or bad for you depending on what you are looking for. Party AI is competent, although I do miss the ability from Origins to set my own AI priorities in greater detail. That said AI does experience some issues with particular class subtrees, but it's not game breaking and chances are you will not notice it unless you try to play on nightmare difficulty without micro managing your party. That brings me to the next point - tactical mode is back and it's quite good. If you are into that kind of thing, you can totally use pause a lot to issue orders to the entirety of your party.

Writing in my opinion is very good this time around and I thoroughly enjoyed the main story as well as companion and side quests. Dialogue trees are good, you have quite a bit of freedom in how you want to play your character.

I'm purposefully omitting multiplayer from this review because in my opinion it's inconsequential to the game experience and should be viewed rather as a free spin off.

I could keep going on about how much of an improvement Inquisition is over DA2, and how good it is on its own, but I want to cut this review short with just this recommendation: of you are an RPG fan or just enjoy a good story, pick this up and play.

author: nomaddc
quote:
A good example of a fun and good MMORPG getting ruined for the sake of extracting every single conceivable penny out of the player base. The game is fun and looks amazing with a few caveats.

Updates to old classes are rare. They mostly focus on freshly released classes and make sure they are in a good spot balance-wise and get new paid outfits (although even this was in decline lately). Older classes get largely neglected (DK, Valk, War, Kuno, Maehwa, Tamer, Ranger) and rarely get any fixes or costumes.

Events have been using lots of recycled old rewards, rarely we get anything substantially new for Christmas/Halloween/etc.. It's mostly stuff from several years ago.

Enhancing. It's the only means of gear progression (besides just buying what other people enhance for disproportionally more) and it's made to be as frustrating and infuriating as possible. It's made to irritate and frustrate the player to the point when buying some outfits to melt for enhancing "protection" starts to sound like a great idea. This is where they try to milk you dry. Repairing gear? 1 memory fragment restores 1/100 durability, unless you buy with $$ some Artisan Memories, and even then it takes a good amount. Upgrading past DUO? Gear will downgrade on failing unless you use Cron Stones ("protection") that you either get from melting paid outfits or buy using silver (although it's much worse ratio than buying outfits from the market that other players sell for silver). But even then the conversion rate of $ or your time to crons is awful. Of course, you don't have to spend a dime on any of this, but what people forget to say is that your experience with the game will vary depending on how much you spend. If you don't spend odds are it will be miserable. Alternatively, you can elect to upgrade your gear using Caphras stones, but this will take disproportionately longer than enhancing to the point of not really being viable.

If they introduced more fail protection to enhancing and reduced Cron Stone prices from in-game vendors to make them worth buying over outfit melting it would improve the game a lot. If they started releasing new outfits and balance changes for older classes instead of having Artisans memory sales it would make BDO a really good MMORPG.

I would not advise getting anywhere near this game if you are an impulsive person or have gambling problems - it will attempt to exploit you at every turn.

author: nomaddc
quote:
One of the greatest free to play games of our time, and most fair one. Warframe does not indulge in questionable and manipulative business practices a lot of other free to play developers do, it keeps monetisation fair and simple, clearly communicated and it's economy is player driven.

When picking up Warframe one should keep in mind a few things.
- It's a BIG game. There is lots of stuff to do, lots of places to go, lots of game systems. It's easy to get overwhelmed if you rush too much and don't bide your time getting acquainted with said game systems.
- It is a loot-centered game, in a sense spiritually similar to likes of Diablo, Destiny and many others. To get cool stuff you need to grind for it. That's the main gameplay loop, and there is no way (except platinum, but later on that) around it. You probably won't like it if you want everything given to you right away or with minimal effort.
- Don't get turned off by platinum as fast. It is not exclusively obtained with real money as many ppl are conditioned to expect in modern gaming. Platinum can be traded freely between players for in-game items. That's where player driven market comes into play. You are free to trade with other players for platinum in exchange for mods, prime parts and other stuff you got. It is totally possible to obtain "platinum exclusive" unlocks and purchases without investing a dime into Warframe. It is really up to player's choice. While it may be tough very early on to obtain items of value, you will be able to get some pretty soon (depending on the pace at which you complete quests and learn the game). Plenty and more opportunities to make some platinum once you get a solid grasp of game's basics.
- In addition to that (or if you think it's too much work) - game generously awards you with 75% platinum discounts every so often, and that platinum will last you a long time if you don't go spending it carelessly (or on easily farmable resources).
- Don't get overly obsessed with "prime" stuff. Some of it may not be available at "this time right here and now" and you may have to wait or trade with other players to get it. It may be pretty expensive (platinum wise). But the point many new players miss is that you don't *need* prime stuff to participate in end-game activities. Is it marginally better? Yes. Does it look cooler? Up to personal taste. Do you *need* it? No, this feeling is called "want", not "need". Can you obtain it eventually? Most certainly yes! (except the only and one founders exclusive Excalibur prime and 2 weapons that came with it, but there is something else for excalibur fans, much cooler)
- To expand on last point - prime stuff gets removed from loot tables every now and then, so you can't farm it anymore. Then it gets added back for some time again every so often, so everyone who missed it can get it again without utilizing player trading. Combined with the point about difference between "need" and "want" - you can either wait for it to become available again or trade with other players to get it here and now. It's entirely up to you to decide how much it's worth to you personally, and if you should wait or trade. If you think it's not worth platinum players asking for it - don't buy it off them, just wait. Inevitably it will be dropping once more and drop in price as well.

Overall it's an amazing game that truly shows how much a free to play game can achieve without resorting to manipulation, gambling and moral bankruptcy.
It is definitely far from done yet, there may be some bugs every now and then (that so to say get fixed rapidly with hotfixes), there may be some gameplay elements that could be better (and surprise - they do get better as game goes on, for example movement 1.0 vs movement 2.0 update).
I had this game on my radar since it's early days and looking back at the path behind leaves me immensely impressed. From really modest beginnings it got where it is, and it leaves me only more excited for what's to come.

My advice - give this game a fair chance to grow on you, and it most likely will. If you find out you're not into games of this type - you lose nothing since it's free, but you've at least tried the best game of this type out there.

author: nomaddc
quote:
I'll try to keep it organized. I've played the game up until march 2017 since, well, release I suppose. Story wise expansion is great. That's good news. Bad news: good news end here.

Legion has introduced new levels of RNG walls, class simplification and content recycling. Prepare to experience the wonders of grinding for AP and legendaries, doing repetitive World Quests, and visiting same dungeons over and over again, but this time forced to go there, as best AP and out-of-raids gear can only be obtained there.

To sweeten the pot - chance to get what you actually want in those mythic+ dungeons is extremely low (instead of individual loot pools from each boss you only get 1-2 items from doing the whole thing, so chances to get particular item drop through the ground, not even to mention that most of the time you need that item to "roll high" - get a sufficient titanforged bonus for it to actually be good for you, which adds another layer of rng on top of already awful rng wall.

Grinding for legendaries is another plague that was added with Legion. If you harbor hopes of doing any high-end content - prepare to grind day and night, unless you are one of those lucky persons who win big in casinos in first hour: getting throughput legendaries that are not junk will require you to sell your very soul to RNG gods. Out of pool of ~8 possible legendaries (for the time when I quit) normally only 2-3 are really good, rest varying from semi-decent to "burn and scatter that trash right now", really depending on class. This also not only impacts directly your chances to be taken into a good progression group (also directly linking your luck to how well you can perform - without right legendaries you will never get close to other players who have them, and so you will be quite likely turned down by many progress raiding teams). Not to mention that you should probably give up any hopes of playing your alts - if going through legendary and AP grinding hell on main wasn't enough, you can always opt to repeat it on your alt and sink another sizable chunk of your life into this frustration fueled experience.

This expansion is totally not alt friendly for said reasons: grinding AP, grinding legendaries, and the fact that thanks to lack of weekly lockout on mythic+ time you spend on your alt is time you could spend improving your main (and potentially getting that one sweet, sweet legendary). If you are in a progression/mythic oriented guild - you will always be reminded that you should be grinding on your raiding character instead of having fun with alts.

Definition of "Legendary" items has reached new bottom: not it's not just rather ordinary to receive a "Legendary!" item, now it also can be disappointing and frustrating!

Players that stay for longer periods of time are the ones that are getting hurt by new Blizzard course the most. Currently game is strongly oriented towards "seasonal" players: players who come for a few weeks every time new content is released, only to abandon game until next content influx. If you are kind of player who sticks around from patch to patch.
Prepare to be frustrated by the game, and prepare to be disappointed every time you see that one friend of yours (who doesn't even really remember what's going on plot-wise) log in for a few days when new content is out to "check it out" only to luck out and get his best in slot legendaries and high titanforged items, then snarky remark that "lol, that's all content?", and proceed with quitting until next patch, while you still don't have the legendary you want half a year after launch and doing content weekly since then.

Prepare to grind your soul out trying to get your hidden artifact appearance (especially Combat "aka Outlaw" rogue one. Really, good luck with that, I've personally met ppl who have ran both of those dungeons over 400 times each, and I myself ran them over 150 times without getting anything). Prepare to hear how some random guildie will get one on his alt and never use it, or laugh in chat about how easy it was.

Classes have devolved even further, under false pretense of "trimming"/"pruning"/making them "fun" to play. Instead of fun you get flashiness and instant gratification centered gameplay with little depth to it and low skill ceiling (even MoP/Cata were better in that). Some classes stay broken months into expansion without any improvement (promises that "it's coming soon" don't count) - look up hunters ever since legion launched, or warlocks.

Overall I would place Legion among worst expansions World of Warcraft ever had, even more so because things it did get *really good* get simply crossed out by how frustrating and grindy game has become. Yes, story is good. Yes, raiding is somewhat solid. Yes, mythic+ is fun to do, but only at first. Yes, introduction of appearance collections and sets is welcome. But all of it gets totally overshadowed by how much game has degraded in its very core aspects.

author: nomaddc
quote:
Regulation 1.06 was announced to be released on April 28, and it was to fix some serious Online issues. But in reality it never arrived, but what's even worse - Bandai Namco didn't release any official statement on why Regulations didn't arrive and when they will, as well as there is complete silence on this subject on Dark Souls twitter or in steam news/announcements/community. It's already May 6, and official Dark Souls channels are behaving like if nothing happened at all. Patch did arrive on consoles though, but not PC.

That and the fact that game is still laggy on high-end rigs, drops frames, has gameplay issues (try look up "Poise Dark Souls 3" or "Darkmoon blades wait time PC") that need to be addressed, really ambiguous patch notes in past (instead of being precise on what was fixed or changed, they just roll with "graphics were adjusted" or "Long sword damage was tuned". And that's not touching biggest part - combat. Many unique weapons from previous games made it, but their movesets are now complete garbage, there are about 2 variation of moveset across whole weapon classes, many unique and cool movesets are gone, the final boss soul weapon is absolutely disappointing as it is pretty much a reskin of very basic weapon that can be obtained rather early in the game with minor change (weapon art, which is also extremely disappointing). Overall weapons are bland and boring, Twinblade weapon class is gone, some categories have only 3 weapons (while in previous games it was more, and weapons were more unique).

Because of all this my score is 0/10. Once we get some official statement on Regulation 1.06 (and apology to Dark Souls community), Blue Sentinels and Darkmoon blades covenants fixed, and at least get rid of random fps drops on hi-end PCs - I will reconsider this score. Until then - here it is.
